about: Router Home known-vulnerability list (GL.iNet security notices turned into checks). Signed with the Router Home release key; routers ignore a copy whose signature doesn't match. Format: docs/VULN-CHECKER.md in the Router Home project.

advisories.title: GL.iNet cloud remote management was exploited to install malware
advisories.summary: An unauthorized party used a vulnerability in GL.iNet's cloud remote management services to install malicious software on some GL.iNet routers and KVM devices. GL has blocked that attack path, so devices can't be newly infected through it, but that doesn't remove malware from devices that were already infected. GL's sign of infection: a running process containing "crond -i /tmp/.log".
advisories.firmware_note: Fixed in GL's stable security firmware of 2026-11-22: 4.9.1 for the Brume 3 (GL-MT5000) and 4.10.2 for the Flint 3 (GL-BE9300), per GL's release notes ("fixes a vulnerability in the cloud platform's remote management"; also kernel patches for CVE-2026-98432 and CVE-2026-99288). Other models: install GL's stable update from 2026-11-22 or later when the Upgrade page offers it, even if this check finds nothing.
advisories.indicators_note: List v5 (2026-11-24): besides GL's own sign, traces published by independent researchers who examined affected routers (RemoteToHome-io/gl-security-incident-2026 on GitHub, plus the community triage script admonstrator/glinet-csa-2026-01). GL.iNet hasn't confirmed these. Traces in /tmp and the running programs disappear when the router restarts; the backdoor files survive restarts and firmware upgrades with Keep settings.

indicators.label: The malware process "crond -i /tmp/.log" is running (GL's sign of infection)
A hidden backdoor program (monitord) is running
A hidden backdoor program (ujaild) is running
A remote-control connection to the attackers' server is running
The router is connecting to the attackers' server (170.39.226.x)
The backdoor file /bin/ulogd exists (it isn't part of GL's firmware)
A startup file (urandom_seed) was changed to launch the backdoor
The backdoor was set to survive firmware upgrades
An attacker's SSH key (named gl-agent) can sign in
An attacker's SSH key (named gl-agent) can sign in
The remote terminal (rtty) points to an attackers' server
A startup script contacts an attackers' server
A scheduled task contacts an attackers' server
A firewall rule left behind by the attack's remote command is present
A pipe file /tmp/f exists (used by the attack's remote shell; the name is generic, so not proof on its own)
A hidden file /tmp/.log exists (the malware's file; not proof on its own)

exposures.label: GoodCloud remote management is turned on (the service that was exploited)

advice.infected: Treat this router as hacked. Don't restart it yet if you want to keep evidence (a restart erases some traces). Then reinstall GL's latest official firmware with "Keep settings" turned OFF (a plain factory reset doesn't remove a backdoor that was set to survive upgrades and doesn't install the fix), set the router up again by hand without restoring a backup from it, use a new admin password, and change the passwords and keys of VPNs and accounts used through it. Leave GoodCloud remote management off unless you need it.
advice.suspicious: A trace that matches this attack was found, but it isn't proof on its own (a file or rule with the same name can have an innocent cause). Run the check again; if anything stronger shows up, treat the router as hacked. If you don't recognise it, the safe choice is to reinstall GL's latest firmware with "Keep settings" turned off.
advice.update: No sign of infection, but this router's firmware is older than GL's security fix for this issue. Install the update from the Upgrade page (use the Home tab's firmware checklist first; Router Home survives with Keep settings).
advice.exposed: No sign of infection, but the exploited service is on. GL has blocked the attack path; turning remote management off until the security firmware is installed removes the risk entirely. You can turn it back on in GL's Applications > GoodCloud page later.
advice.ok: No signs of infection and GoodCloud remote management is off. GL still recommends installing the stable security firmware when it's offered.

advisories.title: GL.iNet security advisories of Nov 24: NAS login bypass, remote terminal (rtty) root access and two more
advisories.summary: GL.iNet published four vulnerabilities (no CVE numbers or severity given): a login bypass in GL's NAS sharing service gl_nas_sys (vdb-submit-1113491), root access through the remote terminal (rtty) settings with a TLS certificate check bypass (vdb-submit-1112986), a root command injection in the AstroWarp API (vdb-submit-1112997) and an EMQX authorization bypass leading to remote code execution (vdb-submit-1112985, used on GL's KVM devices). GL's advice: upgrade to the firmware that contains the fixes. GL lists no sign of infection and no factory reset.
advisories.firmware_note: Fixed in 4.9.2 for the Brume 3 (GL-MT5000), per GL's release notes ("Fixed vulnerability VDB-submit-1113491 and enhanced the security protection of NAS identity authentication"). GL's table of fixed versions for other models doesn't line up on their page, so other models aren't listed here yet: install the update GL offers on the Upgrade page from 2026-11-24 or later. Router Home also reads GL's release notes and shows "Firmware update needed" when a new firmware for your model describes security fixes.

advice.update: This router's firmware is older than GL's fix. Install the update from the Upgrade page (use the Home tab's firmware checklist first; Router Home survives with Keep settings). Until then, if you don't use them, turn off NAS sharing (GL's Applications > Network Storage page) and GoodCloud's remote terminal.
advice.ok: This router's firmware has GL's fix, or GL hasn't confirmed a fixed version for this model yet. If GL's Upgrade page offers an update dated 2026-11-24 or later, install it; until then, turn off NAS sharing and GoodCloud's remote terminal if you don't use them.
